Done. T2 solved in one execution, no failures.

**What the script does** (`out/T2/solution.py`):

- Builds two index vectors once: kept qkv rows `0..3839 ⧺ 4608..6143` (head 5 = rows `768*5 .. 768*5+767`) and kept dense columns `0..1279 ⧺ 1536..2047` (head 5 = columns `256*5 .. 256*5+255`).
- Streams all 244 tensors from `inputs/base/model.safetensors` with `safe_open`, slicing `query_key_value.weight`/`.bias` along dim 0 and `attention.dense.weight` along dim 1; everything else is copied through unchanged, names untouched.
- Fails loudly before writing: input tensor count, per-tensor input shapes, no dtype drift, match counts (32 qkv tensors and 16 dense weights across 16 layers — catches an over- or under-matching pattern), the three required layer-0 shapes, output count of 244, plus the same shape check on all 16 layers. After `save_file` it reopens the output and re-verifies the count and the three shapes.

**Output:** `out/T2/model.safetensors`, 244 tensors, 1.9 GB, float16 preserved along with the input's metadata header.

The one thing worth flagging as the real trap in this task: the GPT-NeoX fused projection interleaves q/k/v *inside* each head's 768-row block, so head 5 is a single contiguous row span. Reading it as `[q | k | v]` segments would produce a checkpoint with exactly the right shapes but garbage attention — which is why the checks are on exact shapes and match counts rather than just "something shrank". `out/T2/REPORT.md` records this and the other pitfalls per the template.
